system.name: Astro
system.description: Astro, the web framework for content-driven websites: the framework and its CLI, the component compiler and render runtime, the official integrations and deployment adapters, create-astro, the upgrade tool and the language tools.

corpus.included: The whole withastro/astro repository at the revision below and its history since 2026-05-25, read only: packages/, examples/, the root configuration, .github/, .agents/, .changeset/, benchmark/, scripts/ and reference/.
corpus.excluded: Dependencies (node_modules), generated output (dist/, .astro/) and secrets. The Astro compiler, Starlight and the docs site live in other repositories and are not in the corpus.

consumers.name: Site developer
consumers.description: A developer who builds a website with Astro: starts the project, writes its pages, components and content, runs it locally, builds it and deploys it to a host.

consumers.name: Integration author
consumers.description: A developer who writes an integration, deployment adapter, content loader or toolbar app that other Astro developers install.

consumers.name: Vite app developer
consumers.description: A developer who renders Astro components from their own server code in a Vite project, without Astro's pages, routing or CLI.

providers.name: Astro
providers.description: The Astro framework and the tools around it, as developers use them.

parts.name: Deployment adapters
parts.why: Adapters to hosting platforms (packages/integrations/node, vercel, netlify, cloudflare): how the Site framework reaches each platform's output format, functions, image and cache services; variants of the AstroAdapter contract, not components by themselves.

parts.name: UI framework integrations and renderers
parts.why: Adapters to UI framework libraries (packages/integrations/react, preact, solid, svelte, vue and packages/renderers/*): each pairs the framework's Vite plugin with a renderer that fulfils the AstroRenderer contract.

parts.name: Content format integrations
parts.why: Adapters to the MDX and Markdoc libraries (packages/integrations/mdx, markdoc), added through the Integration API as page and content entry types.

parts.name: Markdown processors
parts.why: Libraries that turn Markdown into HTML (packages/markdown/satteri, the default, and packages/markdown/remark), two variants of the MarkdownProcessor contract chosen by markdown.processor.

parts.name: Feature integrations
parts.why: Adapters to libraries or libraries the developer calls: sitemap (the sitemap library), partytown, alpinejs, @astrojs/rss (rss() returns a Response from an endpoint) and @astrojs/prism.

parts.name: Shared helpers
parts.why: Libraries other packages import (packages/internal-helpers, packages/underscore-redirects).

parts.name: Retired integration stubs
parts.why: packages/integrations/deno, web-vitals and tailwind hold only a README or changelog; see cleanup candidates.

components.name: Site framework
components.description: The astro package: it sets up a project, runs the dev and preview servers, builds the site and answers requests for its pages.

parts.name: astro CLI
parts.why: A client that passes each command to the part that runs it (packages/astro/src/cli/index.ts); info, docs and create-key only print, open a URL or generate a value. Part of the astro CLI interface.

parts.name: npm registry client
parts.why: An adapter to the npm registry (packages/astro/src/cli/install-package.ts) used by astro add, astro check and the dev server's update check.

parts.name: Dev toolbar
parts.why: A browser client that presents the dev server's view of the page, with audits and the toolbar app API (packages/astro/src/runtime/client/dev-toolbar/, src/toolbar/). Part of the dev toolbar interface.

parts.name: Container API
parts.why: It passes a component render on to the request handler's render path (packages/astro/src/container/index.ts). Part of the Astro APIs interface.

parts.name: Telemetry events
parts.why: Builds event payloads and hands them to Telemetry (packages/astro/src/events/); an adapter.

parts.name: Markdown pages
parts.why: Turns .md page files into page modules with the configured markdown processor (packages/astro/src/markdown/, src/vite-plugin-markdown/); an adapter.

parts.name: Runtime re-exports
parts.why: One-line re-exports of @astrojs/runtime kept so astro/runtime/* imports resolve (packages/astro/src/runtime/server/, runtime/client/*.ts, runtime/compiler/).

parts.name: Shared code
parts.why: Libraries every part imports: types, logger, error definitions and overlay, messages, file and module helpers (packages/astro/src/types/, core/logger/, core/errors/, core/messages/).

parts.name: Legacy adapter entrypoint
parts.why: Supports deprecated entrypointResolution 'explicit' adapters (packages/astro/src/entrypoints/legacy.ts); a cleanup candidate.

components.name: Project setup
components.description: Resolves the project's config into the settings every part reads, runs the integration hooks, assembles the Vite config and syncs generated types.

parts.name: Config resolution
parts.why: Loads and validates astro.config into the settings (core/config/); shares the settings object with the hooks.

parts.name: Integration hooks
parts.why: The registry through which integrations change the settings (integrations/hooks.ts); writes the same settings object as config resolution.

parts.name: Vite config assembly
parts.why: Builds the Vite config with Astro's plugins (core/create-vite.ts); wiring.

parts.name: Sync
parts.why: Runs content sync and the type generators in order (core/sync/index.ts); passes on.

components.name: Dev server
components.description: Runs the project on a local server that renders pages on request, restarts when the config changes and records itself for astro dev status, logs and stop.

parts.name: Container and restart
parts.why: The running server and its restarts (core/dev/container.ts, restart.ts); the one deciding part.

parts.name: Adapter validation
parts.why: Checks that the adapter supports the features in use (core/dev/adapter-validation.ts); a check.

parts.name: Lockfile
parts.why: Storage: the record of a running server in .astro/dev.json (core/dev/lockfile.ts).

parts.name: Update check
parts.why: Asks the npm registry for the latest Astro through the npm registry client (core/dev/update-check.ts).

parts.name: Dev-only Vite plugins
parts.why: Error overlay client, dev status, Chrome DevTools workspace and dev CSS plugins (vite-plugin-overlay/, vite-plugin-dev-status/, vite-plugin-chromedevtools/, vite-plugin-css/); wiring.

parts.name: Background commands
parts.why: Start, check and stop a background server by reading the lockfile and logs (cli/dev/).

components.name: Preview server
components.description: Serves a finished build locally, through the adapter's preview entrypoint or its own static server.

components.name: Site builder
components.description: Builds the site: bundles client and server code, prerenders static pages, writes the manifest and the output for the adapter.

parts.name: Build orchestration
parts.why: Runs the hooks and the build phases in order (core/build/index.ts); passes on.

parts.name: Bundling
parts.why: Vite builds and their plugins (core/build/static-build.ts, plugins/); they write the shared BuildInternals (core/build/internal.ts).

parts.name: Page generation
parts.why: Renders each static path and writes it (core/build/generate.ts); reads BuildInternals the bundling writes.

parts.name: Incremental build cache
parts.why: Keeps the previous build's manifest to skip unchanged pages (core/build/incremental.ts); its inputs are written into BuildInternals by plugins/plugin-incremental.ts.

parts.name: Prerenderers
parts.why: Variants of AstroPrerenderer that pass each render on to the built app (default-prerenderer.ts, parallel-prerenderer.ts).

parts.name: Timings
parts.why: Build diagnostics (core/build/timings/).

components.name: Request handler
components.description: Answers each request, in development, at build and in production: matches the route, runs redirects, actions and middleware, renders the page or endpoint, applies i18n routing and renders error pages.

parts.name: Routing
parts.why: Route list, route table, matching and rewrites (core/routing/); it shares and changes the per-request FetchState with the other stages.

parts.name: Middleware
parts.why: Loads and runs the middleware chain (core/middleware/); sets locals in FetchState that pages read.

parts.name: Localization
parts.why: i18n redirects, fallbacks and locale helpers (core/i18n/, src/i18n/); reads and changes FetchState.

parts.name: Server islands
parts.why: The island route and name map (core/server-islands/); an endpoint rendered by the same chain.

parts.name: Page rendering
parts.why: Renders the matched page or endpoint through the render runtime (core/pages/, core/render/, core/fetch/fetch-state.ts).

parts.name: Facades
parts.why: App, NodeApp and the astro/fetch and astro/hono handlers pass requests into the chain (core/app/, core/fetch/index.ts, core/hono/).

parts.name: Dev request plugins
parts.why: The Vite middleware and dev App that answer dev requests with the same chain, plus dev error pages (vite-plugin-astro-server/, vite-plugin-app/); they call routing, middleware, rewrites and render directly.

parts.name: Cookies and CSP
parts.why: Helpers for response cookies and Content-Security-Policy headers (core/cookies/, core/csp/).

parts.name: Redirects and rewrites
parts.why: Configured redirects and Astro.rewrite, which re-run the chain on the same FetchState (core/redirects/, core/rewrites/).

components.name: Content layer
components.description: Loads content collections into the data store, answers queries for their entries and generates their types and schemas.

parts.name: Store classes and loader contract
parts.why: Shared code both inner components use: ImmutableDataStore and its sources (content/data-store.ts, data-store-source.ts), which MutableDataStore extends, and the Loader and LiveLoader types and errors (content/loaders/types.ts, errors.ts).

parts.name: Config and helpers
parts.why: Content config loading and shared helpers (content/config.ts, utils.ts, config-prewarm.ts, consts.ts, paths.ts).

parts.name: Content wiring
parts.why: Vite plugins for content imports and assets, and the dev server listeners that feed file changes to sync and type generation (content/vite-plugin-content-imports.ts, vite-plugin-content-assets.ts, server-listeners.ts).

components.name: Content sync
components.description: Runs each collection's loader, writes the entries into the content data store, and generates the collections' types and the schema files editors read.

parts.name: Content layer runner
parts.why: Runs the loaders with their context and keeps the store current (content/content-layer.ts); the deciding part.

parts.name: Types generator
parts.why: Writes content types and collection schemas (content/types-generator.ts); it and the runner both write .astro/collections/collections.json (types-generator.ts writes it, content-layer.ts regenerateCollectionFileManifest rewrites its entries), so they share one store.

parts.name: Data store
parts.why: Storage: the mutable store, its writer and the module that serves it (content/mutable-data-store.ts, data-store-writer.ts, vite-plugin-content-virtual-mod.ts).

parts.name: Loaders
parts.why: glob() and file(), variants of the Loader contract that read the project's files; adapters to storage (content/loaders/glob.ts, file.ts).

parts.name: Watcher
parts.why: Reacts to file changes in dev (content/watcher.ts).

components.name: Collection queries
components.description: Answers getCollection, getEntry, render and the live collection functions from the synced store or from live loaders at request time.

parts.name: Query functions
parts.why: getCollection, getEntry, getEntries, render and the live functions, read-only and request-time (content/runtime.ts, runtime-assets.ts); the deciding part.

components.name: Images
components.description: Optimizes images: decides each transform through the configured image service, serves the image endpoint and writes optimized files at build.

parts.name: getImage and layout
parts.why: Decides each transform, srcset and responsive layout (assets/internal.ts, layout.ts); the deciding part.

parts.name: Image services
parts.why: sharp, noop and adapters' services: adapters to the sharp library and to platform image services (assets/services/).

parts.name: Image endpoint
parts.why: Passes /_image requests on to the service (assets/endpoint/).

parts.name: Build generation
parts.why: Writes optimized images and their cache (assets/build/generate.ts); shares the static image list with getImage.

parts.name: SVG components
parts.why: Turns SVG files into components with svgo (assets/svg/); library use.

components.name: Fonts
components.description: Resolves the configured font families from their providers, downloads and caches their files, and computes fallbacks and preloads.

parts.name: Font resolution
parts.why: Pure functions over the interfaces in definitions.ts that resolve families, fallbacks and preloads (assets/fonts/core/); the deciding part.

parts.name: Font providers
parts.why: Adapters to outside font services, and a local provider (assets/fonts/providers/).

parts.name: Font infrastructure
parts.why: Storage, fetcher and font file readers (assets/fonts/infra/).

components.name: Actions
components.description: Runs the server functions a project defines: validates each call's input, runs the handler and returns the result or error.

parts.name: Action handler
parts.why: Validates input, runs the handler and serializes the result (actions/handler.ts, actions/runtime/server.ts); the deciding part.

parts.name: Browser client
parts.why: Presents actions as functions in the browser (actions/runtime/client.ts); part of the Astro APIs interface.

components.name: Sessions
components.description: Keeps per-visitor session data across requests in the storage the session driver names.

parts.name: AstroSession
parts.why: Reads and changes one visitor's session data (core/session/runtime.ts); the deciding part.

parts.name: Session drivers
parts.why: Adapters to storage (core/session/drivers.ts, driver.ts).

components.name: Response cache
components.description: Caches rendered responses by route rules and tags, through the memory provider or a CDN provider, and invalidates them.

parts.name: Cache handler and route rules
parts.why: Decides what is cached and for how long (core/cache/handler.ts, runtime/route-matching.ts); the deciding part.

parts.name: Cache providers
parts.why: The in-memory store and adapters' CDN providers, variants of CacheProvider (core/cache/memory-provider.ts and the adapters' cache/provider.ts).

components.name: Environment variables
components.description: Validates environment variables against the project's schema and gives pages typed access to public and secret values.

components.name: Preferences
components.description: Keeps the developer's own settings for Astro's tools, per project and global, such as whether the dev toolbar shows.

components.name: Page transitions
components.description: In the browser, fetches the next page and swaps it in place with view transition animations, keeping scroll and history.

components.name: Link prefetching
components.description: In the browser, fetches linked pages ahead of a click, on hover, tap, viewport or load.

components.name: Integration installer
components.description: Adds integrations to a project: installs their packages and edits the config file.

components.name: Component compiler
components.description: The Vite plugin for the Astro component language: compiles .astro files and gives the runtime their renderers, directives, stylesheets and island URLs.

parts.name: Compile plugins
parts.why: The one deciding part: compiles .astro modules and records their metadata (src/internal/vite-plugin-astro/, src/internal/core/compile/).

parts.name: Component assets
parts.why: Derives a tree's stylesheets and island URLs from Vite's module graph and the compile metadata (src/vite-plugin-component-assets/).

parts.name: Virtual module plugins
parts.why: Serve renderers, client directives, scripts and render setup, and handle head propagation and HMR, from the one resolved options object (src/plugin.ts and the vite-plugin-* folders).

parts.name: Options and errors
parts.why: Schema, defaults and error helpers (src/options.ts, src/defaults.ts, src/internal/core/errors/).

components.name: Render runtime
components.description: The code compiled components run with: renders component trees to HTML, hydrates islands in the browser and encrypts server island props.

parts.name: Server rendering
parts.why: The one deciding part: renders trees to HTML and keeps the registered render config (src/internal/server/, src/internal/render-setup.ts).

parts.name: Island hydration scripts
parts.why: Browser scripts that server rendering embeds in each page (src/internal/client/, src/internal/server/astro-island.ts).

parts.name: Transition helpers
parts.why: Event and swap functions the Site framework's router calls (src/internal/transitions/).

parts.name: Errors and helpers
parts.why: AstroError and its definitions, encryption, CSP sources, escaping and JSX runtime; libraries (src/internal/core/, src/jsx-runtime/).

components.name: Language tools
components.description: Editor and type-checking support for .astro files: the language server, its VS Code client, the TypeScript plugin, astro check and the TypeScript 7 content mapper.

parts.name: Language server
parts.why: The one deciding part: diagnostics, completions and formatting for .astro files over LSP (language-server/).

parts.name: VS Code extension
parts.why: A client that starts the language server and the TypeScript plugin (vscode/); part of the editor extension interface.

parts.name: TypeScript plugin and content mapper
parts.why: Adapters of the astro2tsx library to tsserver and to TypeScript 7's content mapper (ts-plugin/, ts-content-mapper/).

parts.name: astro check CLI
parts.why: Passes the run on to the language server's check (astro-check/).

parts.name: yaml2ts
parts.why: A library (yaml2ts/).

components.name: Project scaffolder
components.description: create-astro: creates a new project from a template, installs its dependencies and initializes git.

parts.name: Setup steps
parts.why: Steps of one flow sharing one Context (src/actions/).

parts.name: Messages and shell helpers
parts.why: Output, prompts and process helpers (src/messages.ts, src/shell.ts).

parts.name: Templates
parts.why: The examples/ folders, data the template step downloads.

components.name: Upgrader
components.description: @astrojs/upgrade: finds the project's Astro packages, works out their new versions and installs them.

parts.name: Upgrade steps
parts.why: Steps of one flow sharing one Context (src/actions/).

parts.name: Messages and shell helpers
parts.why: Output, prompts and process helpers (src/messages.ts, src/shell.ts).

components.name: Telemetry
components.description: @astrojs/telemetry: keeps whether this machine sends anonymous usage data, and sends the events when it may.

parts.name: Global config store
parts.why: Storage (src/config.ts).

parts.name: Sender
parts.why: Adapter to the Astro telemetry service (src/post.ts).

parts.name: Project and system info
parts.why: Helpers that build the event context (src/project-info.ts, src/system-info.ts).

outsideServices.name: npm registry
outsideServices.description: The package registry, through its API and the project's package manager.

outsideServices.name: GitHub
outsideServices.description: Hosts the starter templates create-astro downloads, Astro's own examples and third-party repositories.

outsideServices.name: Astro telemetry service
outsideServices.description: Astro's service that stores anonymous usage events.

outsideServices.name: Astro integrations catalog
outsideServices.description: The astro.build API that lists integrations for the dev toolbar.

outsideServices.name: Astro documentation site
outsideServices.description: docs.astro.build, where the upgrade guides live.

outsideServices.name: Web font providers
outsideServices.description: Google Fonts, Bunny, Fontshare, Fontsource and Adobe Fonts, reached through unifont.

outsideServices.name: Remote image hosts
outsideServices.description: Other servers whose images a site optimizes, when allowed by image.domains or image.remotePatterns.

outsideServices.name: Hosting platform
outsideServices.description: Vercel, Netlify or Cloudflare, which run the built site and offer CDN caching and image optimization, reached through their deployment adapters.

outsideServices.name: Session storage
outsideServices.description: The key-value store a session driver writes to, such as Netlify Blobs, Cloudflare KV or Redis.

resources.name: Project
resources.description: An Astro project: its config, integrations, pages, components and content.

resources.name: Page
resources.description: A page, endpoint or redirect the site serves at a URL, from src/pages, an integration or the config.

resources.name: Component
resources.description: An Astro or UI framework component, rendered in a page and possibly hydrated as an island or deferred as a server island.

resources.name: Content collection
resources.description: A named set of entries defined in the content config, filled by a loader and checked against a schema.

resources.name: Content entry
resources.description: One item of a collection: its data, body, rendered HTML, headings and images.

resources.name: Image
resources.description: A local or remote image and its optimized versions.

resources.name: Font family
resources.description: A font family configured for the site, with its files, faces and fallbacks.

resources.name: Action
resources.description: A server function defined in src/actions and called from browser code or a form.

resources.name: Session
resources.description: Server-side data kept for one visitor across requests, identified by a cookie.

resources.name: Cached response
resources.description: A rendered response kept in a cache, with how long it lives and its tags.

resources.name: Environment variable
resources.description: A variable declared in env.schema, typed and marked public or secret, client or server.

resources.name: Site build
resources.description: What astro build writes: static files, prerendered pages, the server bundle and its manifest.

resources.name: Dev server
resources.description: A running local server that renders the project and updates pages as files change.

resources.name: Preference
resources.description: One of the developer's own settings for Astro's tools, per project or global, such as the dev toolbar or telemetry.

resources.name: Renderer
resources.description: A UI framework renderer registered with Astro: its name and its server and client entrypoints.

resources.name: Usage event
resources.description: An anonymous record of a command run, with the project's and system's context.

resources.name: Package
resources.description: An npm package and its published versions and tags.

resources.name: Template
resources.description: A starter project kept in a GitHub repository.

resources.name: Upgrade guide
resources.description: The documentation page for moving a project to a new major version of Astro.

resources.name: Integration listing
resources.description: The list of integrations the dev toolbar suggests.

resources.name: Deployment
resources.description: The site as a hosting platform runs it: static files, server functions or workers, and routes.

interfaces.name: astro CLI
interfaces.description: The astro command: dev, build, preview, sync, add, check, info, preferences, telemetry and the background dev server commands.

interfaces.name: project files and config
interfaces.description: astro.config and the files Astro reads by convention: src/pages, src/content.config, src/actions, src/middleware, public/ and the tsconfig presets.

interfaces.name: Astro APIs
interfaces.description: The modules project code imports: astro:content, astro:assets, astro:actions, astro:env, astro:i18n, astro:transitions, astro:prefetch, astro:middleware, astro/container, and the Astro global.

interfaces.name: dev toolbar
interfaces.description: The toolbar Astro adds to pages in the browser during astro dev.

interfaces.name: editor extension
interfaces.description: The Astro VS Code extension and the language server, TypeScript plugin and content mapper behind it.

interfaces.name: create-astro CLI
interfaces.description: npm create astro, which creates a new project.

interfaces.name: upgrade CLI
interfaces.description: npx @astrojs/upgrade, which upgrades a project's Astro packages.

interfaces.name: Integration API
interfaces.description: The AstroIntegration object and its hooks, from astro:config:setup to astro:build:done, including setAdapter and setPrerenderer.

interfaces.name: server runtime API
interfaces.description: What an adapter's server entrypoint calls: astro/app, astro/app/node, astro/fetch, astro/hono and astro/env/setup.

interfaces.name: Loader API
interfaces.description: The Loader and LiveLoader contracts and their context, from astro/loaders.

interfaces.name: toolbar app API
interfaces.description: defineToolbarApp and the server helpers for dev toolbar apps, from astro/toolbar.

interfaces.name: Vite plugin
interfaces.description: astro() from @astrojs/vite-plugin-astro, with its options and the renderer packages.

interfaces.name: render API
interfaces.description: renderToString, renderToResponse and createRenderer from @astrojs/runtime.

interfaces.name: astro() plugin API
interfaces.description: astro(options, cli) and getAstroApi, with the AstroPluginCli fields and the plugin's declared internal modules.

interfaces.name: render runtime API
interfaces.description: @astrojs/runtime/server and the runtime's declared internal modules for rendering, encryption, render scope and transitions.

interfaces.name: render setup module
interfaces.description: virtual:astro:render-setup, which registers the compiler's render config with setRenderConfig.

interfaces.name: @astrojs/check API
interfaces.description: check() and parseArgsAsCheckConfig() of @astrojs/check.

interfaces.name: collection schema files
interfaces.description: .astro/collections/collections.json and the JSON schema of each content collection.

interfaces.name: AstroTelemetry API
interfaces.description: The AstroTelemetry class: record, notify, setEnabled, clear.

interfaces.name: npm registry API
interfaces.description: The registry's package metadata endpoints, asked directly or through the package manager.

interfaces.name: integrations catalog API
interfaces.description: GET https://astro.build/api/v1/dev-overlay/.

interfaces.name: font provider APIs
interfaces.description: The providers' font APIs, wrapped by unifont as FontProvider.

interfaces.name: HTTP image fetch
interfaces.description: Plain HTTP requests for remote images, limited to allowed domains and patterns.

interfaces.name: platform deployment output
interfaces.description: Each platform's build output format, written by its adapter: Vercel's .vercel/output, Netlify's functions, Cloudflare's worker and wrangler config.

interfaces.name: platform cache API
interfaces.description: Each platform's CDN cache headers and purge call, used by the adapters' cache providers.

interfaces.name: platform image service
interfaces.description: Each platform's image optimization endpoint or binding, used by the adapters' image services.

interfaces.name: session driver
interfaces.description: The unstorage driver that session.driver names.

interfaces.name: GitHub repository archives
interfaces.description: Repository downloads through giget, such as github:withastro/astro#examples/<name>.

interfaces.name: docs website
interfaces.description: The pages of docs.astro.build.

interfaces.name: telemetry API
interfaces.description: POST https://telemetry.astro.build/api/v1/record.

interfaces.name: project setup functions
interfaces.description: resolveConfig, createSettings, the runHook functions of the integration hooks, createVite and syncInternal.

interfaces.name: dev request plugins
interfaces.description: vitePluginAstroServer and vitePluginApp, the Vite middleware and dev App the dev server's Vite server runs, and createRoutesList.

interfaces.name: build app
interfaces.description: renderForPrerender, StaticPaths, createRoutesList, the manifest serializers, and the routing and rendering helpers the builder calls to plan the build.

interfaces.name: content layer API
interfaces.description: globalContentLayer.init with a MutableDataStore the caller loads, ContentLayer sync and watch, attachContentServerListeners and createContentTypesGenerator.

interfaces.name: image generation API
interfaces.description: prepareAssetsGenerationEnv, generateImagesForPath and StaticImageRegistry.

interfaces.name: fonts plugin and sync
interfaces.description: The fonts Vite plugin and syncFonts.

interfaces.name: env plugin and sync
interfaces.description: The astro:env Vite plugin, its validators and syncAstroEnv.

interfaces.name: action handler
interfaces.description: handleAction and the action helpers on the API context.

interfaces.name: session provider
interfaces.description: provideSession and the AstroSession methods.

interfaces.name: cache handler
interfaces.description: provideCache, handleCache, provideAndHandleCache and the Astro.cache object.

interfaces.name: AstroPreferences
interfaces.description: The preferences object: get, set, getAll, list.

interfaces.name: content image helpers
interfaces.description: imageSrcToImportId and createSvgComponent, and the image() schema helper.

interfaces.name: data store module
interfaces.description: The serialized content data store that content sync's virtual module plugin serves, read through ImmutableDataStore, the class MutableDataStore extends.

areas.name: Build sites
areas.description: Make a website: start the project, develop it locally, write its pages, islands and content, and build it for a host.

capabilities.name: Start project
capabilities.takes: a project name and a template, such as basics, blog, Starlight or a GitHub repository
capabilities.gives: a new project folder with its dependencies installed and a git repository

capabilities.name: Add integration
capabilities.takes: integration names, such as react, mdx or vercel
capabilities.gives: their packages installed and the config updated to use them

capabilities.name: Start dev server
capabilities.takes: the project, optionally to run in the background, as the CLI does by itself when a coding agent runs it
capabilities.gives: a local URL that renders the pages and updates them as files change

capabilities.name: Check background dev server
capabilities.takes: the project
capabilities.gives: whether its dev server is running, its URL, and its logs

capabilities.name: Stop dev server
capabilities.takes: the project
capabilities.gives: its background dev server stopped

capabilities.name: Render pages
capabilities.takes: pages and endpoints in src/ written in .astro, Markdown, MDX or Markdoc, their layouts and middleware, and a request for a URL

questions.question: Are the visitors of a site built with Astro consumers of Astro?
questions.answer: Left out, rather than a Level 1 consumer of the request handler, page transitions and prefetching; visitors use the developer's website and do not know Astro is behind it, so the request-time features appear as capabilities the site developer uses. No rule says how to treat the users of what a framework builds.

questions.question: Are the language tools, create-astro and the upgrade tool providers of their own?
questions.answer: Surfaces of the one provider Astro, rather than separate products; each ships separately (VS Code Marketplace, npm) but keeps no data of its own and serves the same site developers. The rule names deployment, data and consumers but not how many of the three make a separate product.

questions.question: Is the integration author a consumer of its own?
questions.answer: A separate consumer, rather than the site developer using another interface, because published integrations and adapters serve other developers (the Deno adapter and web-vitals moved to other organizations); a developer's local integration uses the same API, and no rule settles a contract used both ways.

questions.question: Is the Vite app developer a consumer of its own?
questions.answer: A separate consumer, rather than the site developer, because the goal (render components from one's own server, with no pages or routing) and the interfaces (astro() and @astrojs/runtime) differ; both write .astro components.

questions.question: Should the request handler open into routing, middleware, localization, server islands and page rendering?
questions.answer: Kept closed, rather than opened, because its stages share and change one per-request FetchState and import each other both ways; routing and middleware each keep per-manifest state behind accessors (core/README.md), which would support opening it.

questions.question: Should the site builder open into bundling, page generation and the incremental build cache?
questions.answer: Kept closed, rather than opened, because the bundler plugins, the incremental plugin and page generation all write or read BuildInternals (core/build/internal.ts); the incremental cache alone keeps the previous build's manifest, which would support making it a component.

questions.question: Are Content sync and the content types generator one component?
questions.answer: One component, rather than two, because both write .astro/collections/collections.json (types-generator.ts writes it, content-layer.ts regenerateCollectionFileManifest rewrites its entries); otherwise they have separate contracts (ContentLayer.sync and createContentTypesGenerator).

questions.question: Where does the seam between content sync and collection queries sit, given that MutableDataStore extends ImmutableDataStore?
questions.answer: At the serialized data store module, with ImmutableDataStore placed in the parent Content layer as shared code, rather than inside either side; the request-time side never imports the mutable store's methods, only its type in one plugin.

questions.question: Are the deployment adapters and UI framework integrations components?
questions.answer: Not components, as the brief and use-boundary-model ask for adapters to outside services and libraries, placed as libraries; read on their own, the adapters are variants of the AstroAdapter contract and could have been one component with variants.

questions.question: Should Vercel, Netlify and Cloudflare be three outside services?
questions.answer: One outside service, Hosting platform, rather than three, because the framework uses the same four things from each (run the build, CDN cache, image transforms, key-value storage for sessions) through variants of the same contracts; three would triple the boundaries without new capabilities.

questions.question: Is a preference a resource, given that the model excludes settings?
questions.answer: A resource, rather than a property of Project, because the developer lists, sets, enables, disables and resets preferences by key through their own commands, and the telemetry setting lives on the machine, not in a project; the setting rule would leave those commands with no resource.

questions.question: Is the sitemap integration a component?
questions.answer: A library, rather than a component, because it maps the build's page list into the sitemap library through two hooks; it does alone write the sitemap files and decide which pages they list, which would let it pass the component test.

questions.question: Are page transitions and link prefetching one component?
questions.answer: Two components, rather than one, because their contracts (astro:transitions/client and astro:prefetch) never call each other; ClientRouter only calls prefetch's init().

questions.question: Do the dev server and builder reach the request handler past its contract?
questions.answer: Accepted as the declared contract, rather than redrawn, by naming in the dev request plugins and build app interfaces the routing, rewrite and render helpers they call; the import graph shows the request path's modules are reached from 40 files elsewhere (work/astro-src-edges.tsv), and nothing in the code enforces the seam beyond the export maps between packages.

questions.question: Do actions, sessions, the response cache and images reach into the request handler?
questions.answer: Accepted, rather than redrawn: they import FetchState, the fetch features registry, cookies and the manifest memo because the request handler calls them with that state; the cache also imports routing's pattern and priority helpers, Actions routing helpers and origin-check, and Images the route parser, which are helper reuse past the contract that a reviewer may prefer to move to shared code.

questions.question: Do the dev server and astro sync reach past the content layer's contract?
questions.answer: Treated as part of the contract, rather than a leak, because globalContentLayer.init takes a MutableDataStore that both callers load themselves with MutableDataStore.fromFile or fromDir (core/dev/dev.ts, core/sync/index.ts); it does put the store's storage format in their hands.

questions.question: Is the telemetry package a component?
questions.answer: A component, rather than storage and an adapter inside the framework, because it keeps its own global store and alone decides what is sent; the preferences README plans to merge the two stores.

cleanupCandidates.name: Retired integration stubs
cleanupCandidates.why: packages/integrations/deno, web-vitals and tailwind keep only a README or changelog saying the package moved to another organization or is deprecated in favor of Tailwind's Vite plugin.

cleanupCandidates.name: Runtime re-export shims
cleanupCandidates.why: packages/astro/src/runtime/server/*, runtime/client/{idle,load,media,only,visible,hmr}.ts and runtime/compiler/index.ts only re-export @astrojs/runtime so the old astro/runtime/* paths keep resolving; the code moved to packages/runtime.

cleanupCandidates.name: Legacy adapter entrypoint and options
cleanupCandidates.why: packages/astro/src/entrypoints/legacy.ts and the deprecated AstroAdapter fields entrypointResolution 'explicit', exports, args and edgeMiddleware support the Astro 5 adapter API (types/public/integrations.ts: 'will be removed in a future major version').

cleanupCandidates.name: App and NodeApp facades
cleanupCandidates.why: core/README.md says they 'survive as thin public compatibility shells' over the functional request core (packages/astro/src/core/app/app.ts, node.ts).

cleanupCandidates.name: remark/rehype markdown pipeline
cleanupCandidates.why: @astrojs/markdown-remark is an optional peer kept for the legacy pipeline; Sätteri is the default processor (types/public/config.ts markdown.processor, knip.js comments).

cleanupCandidates.name: astro check and @astrojs/check
cleanupCandidates.why: astro check prints that it 'will be deprecated in a future Astro release' in favor of @astrojs/ts-content-mapper for TypeScript 7 (packages/astro/src/cli/check/index.ts).

cleanupCandidates.name: Separate telemetry config store
cleanupCandidates.why: @astrojs/telemetry keeps its own global config file, and packages/astro/src/preferences/README.md says the two need to be merged.

cleanupCandidates.name: Deprecated getContainerRenderer root exports
cleanupCandidates.why: The framework integrations' root getContainerRenderer warns that it is deprecated in favor of the /container-renderer entry (packages/integrations/react/src/index.ts and the others).

cleanupCandidates.name: Deprecated prerenderer returns
cleanupCandidates.why: AstroPrerenderer accepts a bare array from getStaticPaths, a bare Response from render and collectStaticImages, all marked deprecated (packages/astro/src/types/public/integrations.ts).

cleanupCandidates.name: legacy.collectionsBackwardsCompat
cleanupCandidates.why: A config flag that keeps the older content collections behavior (packages/astro/src/types/public/config.ts, content/utils.ts).

cleanupCandidates.name: @astro-page: virtual modules
cleanupCandidates.why: architecture.md calls it a 'legacy pattern'; it remains in packages/astro/src/core/build/static-build.ts next to the virtual:astro:* convention.
